title: Review Arcade: On the Human Alignment and Gameability of LLM Reviews
abstract: arXiv:2605.28897v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: LLM-generated reviews for scientific papers are gaining considerable traction and are even being officially piloted by major conferences. We have to assume that not only reviewers are using LLM-assistance, but also that authors use LLMs to revise their papers before submitting. In this work, we perform empirical experiments on accepted and rejected submissions to the 2024-2025 cycles of the ACL Rolling Review (ARR) to evaluate LLM reviews from both the author and the reviewer perspective. First, we identify a limited alignment of LLM reviews with human ones. In the best-case scenario, the alignment is reasonable. However, we also find that LLM-human alignment varies substantially across prompts and models. Finally, we investigate the scenario in which the author uses an iterative draft-revise workflow to improve the submission according to the LLM review. We find that this "gaming" of LLM reviews can be effective in specific scenario

translated_title: Review Arcade：论LLM审稿意见与人类审稿的对齐性及其可博弈性
translated_abstract: LLM生成的科学论文审稿意见正获得越来越多的关注，甚至已被主要学术会议正式试点采用。我们必须假设不仅审稿人在使用LLM辅助，作者也会在投稿前使用LLM修改论文。在这项工作中，我们对2024-2025周期ACL Rolling Review (ARR)的录用和拒稿投稿进行了实证实验，从作者和审稿人两个角度评估LLM审稿意见。首先，我们发现LLM审稿意见与人类审稿意见的对齐程度有限。在最佳情况下，对齐程度尚属合理。然而，我们还发现LLM与人类审稿的对齐程度在不同提示词和模型之间差异很大。最后，我们研究了作者使用迭代起草-修改工作流、根据LLM审稿意见改进投稿的场景。我们发现这种对LLM审稿的“博弈”在特定场景下可能是有效的。
tldr: 该论文通过对ACL Rolling Review录用与拒稿投稿的实证实验发现，LLM审稿意见与人类审稿的对齐程度有限且因提示词和模型而异，同时作者可以通过迭代修改论文的方式有效“博弈”LLM审稿系统。
en_tdlr: This paper empirically shows, using ACL Rolling Review submissions, that LLM reviews only partially align with human reviews (varying substantially across prompts and models), and that authors can effectively "game" LLM reviews through an iterative draft-revise workflow.
